processing_steps_notes.value: Cold rolled with 20% reduction achieved by multipass rolling on a twin roll mill (Φ160), denoted 'CR20%'. The 20% reduction eliminates some micropores caused by solidification shrinkage and avoids great influence on the structure of the steel strips.

source.reason: Overall description of the CR20% 6Cr steel strip's phase assemblage and microstructure from XRD, SEM and TEM results.

overall_structure.value: Cold-rolled (CR20%) near-rapidly solidified low-density Fe-20Mn-9Al-1.2C-6Cr steel strip. The constituent phases are still γ-austenite and δ-ferrite with ordered DO3 phase after cold rolling, completely consistent with the as-cast steel strips. Irregularly shaped δ-ferrite distributes in the γ-austenite matrix; Cr addition makes the short rod-shape ferrite change into block/vermicular ferrite, and cold rolling does not significantly change the morphology or volume fraction of δ-ferrite. Nano-scale κ-carbides precipitate in the austenite and ordered DO3 phase in the δ-ferrite.

number_of_phases.value: 3 (γ-austenite, δ-ferrite, ordered DO3; plus nano-scale κ-carbide in austenite)

source.reason: The CR20% strips consist of γ-austenite matrix with {111} planar slip bands and nano-scale κ-carbides; κ-carbide content decreases with Cr addition.

Discussion of why Cr-containing CR20% strips have higher strength, linking slip band spacing to dislocation blocking.

interaction_type.value: high-density slip bands blocking dislocation movement

qualitative_or_quantitative_description.value: There is a higher density of slip bands in the Cr-containing cold-rolled steel strips than in the Cr-free cold-rolled steel strips. The high-density slip bands significantly block the movement of dislocations and increase the deformation difficulty, which leads to an increase in strength of the Cr-containing steel strips. The smaller the slip band spacing, the greater the stress required for deformation.

slip_behavior.value: {111} planar slip bands are present in the austenite of the CR20% steel strips. The average spacing of the slip bands in the CR20% 6Cr steel strip is 45 ± 13 nm, smaller than the Cr-free (371 ± 47 nm) and 3Cr (100 ± 15 nm) strips, giving a stronger reinforcement effect after cold rolling.

unmapped_findings: Measured composition of the 6Cr steel strip (wt.%): Mn 20.18, Al 9.12, C 1.20, Cr 6.08, S 0.0011, Fe Bal. (Table 1).
Measured average density of the 6Cr steel strip is 6.66 g/cm3 (0Cr 6.71 g/cm3, 3Cr 6.69 g/cm3).
The 0.5 mm from strip surface along the thickness direction was the SEM photography position for microstructure characterization.

As-cast 6Cr condition (not CR20%): the DO3 phase precipitated in the δ-ferrite has a size of 28 ± 4 nm, with no significant change in DO3 size compared with the 3Cr strip; measured lattice parameter of the κ-carbides and γ-austenite is 0.389 nm and 0.384 nm, respectively.

XRD of the CR20% strips: the constituent phases are still γ-austenite and δ-ferrite with ordered DO3 phase after cold rolling, completely consistent with the as-cast steel strips; after further annealing the double-peak changes to a single-peak between 43.5° and 45.0°.
Strain hardening rates of the CR20% steel strips decrease gradually with increasing strain; addition of Cr increases the strain hardening rate of the CR20% steel strips (Fig. 9c, text block b0065).

Annealing the cold-rolled strips (CR20% + annealed, a separate condition) has no significant effect on the yield strength/UTS relative to CR20%, attributed to the high-density slip bands becoming the main strengthening factor.
